howToTell: The Travel Air looks like a smaller Baron but has a tall, upright, squared-off fin; the Baron's fin is swept back and its cabin and engines are larger.
The Duke is a bigger, pressurized six-seater with a rounder fuselage, small rounded windows and large three-blade props; the Baron is smaller and sleeker.
The Aerostar has short, narrow wings, a long slim pointed nose and large rectangular windows; the Baron has a longer tapered wing and a more conventional rounded fuselage.
The Twin Bonanza has big, deep, widely spaced engines and a tall, upright, squared-off fin; the Baron has slim nacelles and a swept fin.
The Twin Comanche is slimmer and sleeker with a sloping nose and a raked fin; the Apache/Aztec is boxier with a thick wing.
The Twin Comanche has an engine on each wing; the single-engine Comanche has one engine in the nose.
The Duchess is a short four-seat T-tail twin; the Seneca has a conventional low tail and a longer six-seat cabin.
Both are T-tail four-seat twins; the Duchess has a rounder Beech-style cabin and smooth nose, while the Seminole's cabin is boxier and PA-28 derived.
The Cougar has a conventional low tail and a smooth rounded fuselage; the Seminole has a T-tail.
The 402 is a bigger, longer-cabin twin seating six to ten; the 310 is smaller and slimmer.
The 402 is unpressurized with a long, straight-sided cabin and larger windows; the 340/414/421 have a portly pressurized cabin with small porthole-like windows.
The Duke has plain wingtips, a smooth round fuselage and a swept fin without a dorsal fillet; the 340 is portly with a dorsal fillet and, on early models, tip tanks.
The 402 has a straighter-sided cabin and, on early models, big wingtip tanks; the Navajo has a tapered wing with plain tips and a dorsal strake on the fin.
The P2006T is a high-wing twin with a conventional low tail; the DA42 is a low-wing composite twin with a T-tail and long slender wings.
The Bobcat is smaller with a single rounded fin and a long glazed canopy; the Beech 18 has twin oval fins.
The DC-6 has four engines and a nose wheel; the DC-3 has two engines and sits on a tailwheel.
The Skymaster has two engines (one in the nose, one pusher behind the cabin) and twin tail booms; the 182 has one engine and a single fin.
The Islander has piston engines, no wing struts and a boxy fuselage with a short nose; the Twin Otter has turboprops, wing struts and a long pointed nose.
The Queen Air has piston cowlings with no exhaust stacks; the King Air has turboprop nacelles with exhaust stacks.
The Commander has a high wing and piston cowlings; the King Air has a low wing and turboprop nacelles with exhaust stacks.
The Cougar has an engine on each wing and a side door; the AA-1/AA-5 has one engine and a sliding canopy.
